Latest Health stories

Health

Thu Nov 5public-health

WHO adds two Bundibugyo-specific Ebola vaccine candidates to Congo trial as cholera also surges

The World Health Organization said on Wednesday that two vaccine candidates designed for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, Oxford and the Serum Institute of India's ChAdOx1 and Moderna's mRNA-1469, will join a clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Thu Nov 5policy

Medicare finalizes 2027 physician pay rule with deeper cuts than proposed

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) on Wednesday finalized its 2027 Physician Fee Schedule, which lowers the main payment rate by 2.31% for most clinicians and 1.83% for those in qualifying advanced payment models, according to Fierce Healthcare.

Thu Nov 5policy

Medicare raises 2027 hospital outpatient rates 2.3% and cuts pay for 340B drugs

CMS on Wednesday finalized a net 2.3% increase in Medicare hospital outpatient payment rates for 2027 and set payment for separately payable drugs bought through the 340B discount program at the average sales price minus 28%, according to the American Hospital Association (AHA).

Mon Nov 2public-health

Congo's Ebola death toll passes 5,000 as Nigeria rules out two suspected cases

Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,000 people, government data reported by Reuters and AP show, and the CDC's latest count lists 10,498 confirmed cases and 5,107 confirmed deaths across affected countries as of October 31.

Mon Nov 2policy

ACA open enrollment begins with benchmark premiums up 13% on average for 2027

Open enrollment for 2027 HealthCare.gov coverage began on November 1 and runs through January 15, 2027, CMS said, and KFF estimates that finalized benchmark silver premiums are rising 13% on average.

Mon Nov 2business

Fresenius signs deal with WuXi Biologics for up to 37 biosimilar candidates

Germany's Fresenius said on Monday it signed an exclusive development agreement with China's WuXi Biologics that gives it access to up to 37 biosimilar candidates over the next decade.

Mon Nov 2regulation

Labor Department publishes rule requiring drug-benefit managers to disclose fees to employer plans

The Labor Department's final rule requiring pharmacy benefit managers to disclose their compensation to fiduciaries of large self-insured employer health plans was published in the Federal Register on Monday.

Sat Oct 31public-health

Congo's Ebola outbreak nears 5,000 deaths, health data show

The Democratic Republic of the Congo had recorded 10,274 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,992 deaths as of Oct. 28, according to its National Institute of Public Health.

Fri Oct 30regulation

FDA proposes updated infant formula nutrient requirements in its first broad review since 1998

The FDA issued a proposed rule on Thursday that would update infant formula requirements for iodine, manganese, vitamin A and vitamin D, the first of three planned proposals in its first comprehensive review of formula nutrients since 1998, HHS said.

Fri Oct 30global-institutions

WHO names seven candidates for its next director-general

The World Health Organization said on Thursday that member states have nominated seven candidates for director-general, with the winner due to take office on August 16, 2027.

Fri Oct 30public-health

WHO certifies Barbados for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV

The World Health Organization said on Friday that Barbados has eliminated mother-to-child transmission of HIV as a public health problem, after no such infections were reported among infants born there from 2022 to 2024.

Thu Oct 29health

Lilly's retatrutide beats Ozempic on blood sugar and weight loss in head-to-head Phase 3 trial

Eli Lilly said its experimental drug retatrutide lowered A1C by an average of 2.2% at 80 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes, compared with 1.8% for Novo Nordisk's Ozempic 2 mg, in the TRANSCEND-T2D-2 trial.

Thu Oct 29health

African health ministers hold emergency Ebola meeting as confirmed cases pass 10,000 in four countries

Africa CDC and the World Health Organization convened African health ministers on Wednesday as the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached 10,172 confirmed cases and more than 4,932 deaths, according to Xinhua and Kenya News Agency.

Wed Oct 28regulation

FDA issues draft guidance for approving personalized gene-editing therapies for rare diseases

The FDA on Tuesday issued draft guidance laying out how sponsors can seek approval for gene-editing therapies tailored to each patient's genetic variant, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) said.

Wed Oct 28science

Artiva halts its autoimmune cell therapy after two trial deaths and cuts 94% of staff

Artiva Biotherapeutics said on Tuesday it is discontinuing development of AlloNK, an off-the-shelf natural killer cell therapy tested with rituximab in rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases, and will not start a planned Phase 3 trial.

Tue Oct 27public-health

Congo's confirmed Ebola cases top 10,000 in its largest outbreak on record

Confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo rose to 10,060, with 4,887 deaths, according to the latest situation report from the country's public health institute, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

Tue Oct 27regulation

FDA approves Pfizer's Talzenna with Xtandi for earlier-stage prostate cancer with HRR mutations

The FDA on October 26 approved talazoparib (Talzenna) with enzalutamide (Xtandi) for adults with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer that carries HRR gene mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test.

Tue Oct 27policy

Medicare's AI-assisted prior authorization pilot cut use of targeted services, JAMA study finds

Use of services covered by Medicare's WISeR prior authorization pilot fell in its six participating states, according to the first study of the program, published in JAMA.

Mon Oct 26public-health

Nigeria's Ebola patient flown to Switzerland as Africa CDC sends scientists to trace her infection

Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, was evacuated from Abuja to Zurich on Monday, while Africa CDC said a team of scientists will investigate how she was infected.

Mon Oct 26science

Divarasib extends survival over current KRAS drugs in Phase 3 lung cancer trial

In the Krascendo 1 trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, Roche's divarasib cut the risk of death by 44% versus sotorasib or adagrasib in previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated lung cancer.

Mon Oct 26public-health

US extends Regeneron Ebola treatment supply deal through 2031

Regeneron said the US Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority expanded a 2020 contract for its Ebola drug Inmazeb, adding about $270 million in payments for doses through 2031.

Sun Oct 25public-health

Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from Congo

Uganda will require citizens returning with a history of travel to Congo to quarantine for 21 days at their own expense, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said Sunday, as it tightens Ebola precautions.

Fri Oct 23public-health

First Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda airport

Africa CDC is investigating whether the first confirmed Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria met at Uganda's Entebbe airport on Oct. 3, as the outbreak that began in Congo spreads.

Fri Oct 23public-health

US measles cases reach 4,588 this year, up 178 in a week

CDC data show 4,588 confirmed US measles cases as of Oct. 22, with 479 hospitalizations and 43 new outbreaks reported in 2026.

Fri Oct 23science

Moderna-Merck personalized melanoma vaccine cuts recurrence risk 42% in Phase 3 trial

Full INTerpath-001 results show intismeran plus Keytruda lowered the risk of melanoma returning or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone after about two years.

Fri Oct 23science

Study estimates summer heat killed more than 50,000 in Europe's cities

Researchers estimate 50,391 heat-related deaths in 854 European cities from June to August 2026, about two-thirds of them linked to human-caused climate change.

Fri Oct 23public-health

France reports first known human case of livestock Shamonda virus

French officials said a severely immunocompromised patient who died in early October had the first documented human Shamonda infection, and said there is no current risk to the public.

modals.2026-10-23-health-1:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Health Digest · public-health

First Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda airport

Both patients traveled through Entebbe International Airport on Oct. 3, Africa CDC emergency response head Wessam Mankoula said Thursday, according to AP. Officials are racing to trace contacts as the Bundibugyo virus outbreak reaches more countries.

Nigeria confirmed its first case on Oct. 20, a woman in Abuja with recent travel to Uganda, making it the fifth country to detect the virus since Congo declared the outbreak on May 15, WHO said. Nigeria has identified 44 contacts. Kenya has reported nine confirmed cases, including one death, all linked to its first case, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. Congo has reported 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths.

Why it matters: Cases tied to air travel through a regional hub widen the contact-tracing effort. ECDC rates the risk to people living in Europe as very low.

modals.2026-10-23-health-2:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Health Digest · public-health

US measles cases reach 4,588 this year, up 178 in a week

The CDC's weekly update counted 4,588 confirmed cases across 47 jurisdictions as of Oct. 22, including 18 among international visitors. Reuters reported the total was up 178 from a week earlier. About 96% of cases are linked to outbreaks.

Pennsylvania has reported 1,317 cases as of Oct. 21, according to state data cited by Reuters. The state health department has reported five measles-related deaths this year, while the CDC has confirmed three. Children and teens aged 5 to 19 are the largest group, at 42% of cases.

Why it matters: Measles is highly contagious, and the weekly rise shows the outbreak is still growing. The CDC has said it would send more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate.

References

  1. Measles Cases and Outbreaks
    CDC · tools.cdc.gov · 2026-10-23
  2. US CDC says measles cases rise to 4,588 as outbreak continues
    Reuters · ksl.com · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-23-health-3:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Health Digest · science

Moderna-Merck personalized melanoma vaccine cuts recurrence risk 42% in Phase 3 trial

Merck and Moderna released detailed results from the 1,137-patient Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial in people whose stage IIB-IV melanoma had been surgically removed. After a median 24.6 months, adding the individualized mRNA therapy intismeran autogene to Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38%, the companies said. Two-year recurrence-free survival was 82.2% versus 70.0%. Overall survival data are not yet mature.

The data, set for the ESMO congress in Madrid, came out early after an embargo breach. Moderna shares closed down 15.6% on Thursday as some figures came in below earlier-stage results, Clinical Trials Arena reported. The companies said they are talking with regulators.

Why it matters: The trial is a major late-stage test of tailor-made mRNA cancer vaccines, each built from a patient's own tumor. The results have been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine.

    Merck · merck.com · 2026-10-23
  2. ESMO26: MSD and Moderna drop cancer vaccine trial data early
    Clinical Trials Arena · clinicaltrialsarena.com · 2026-10-23
  3. Moderna mRNA vaccine almost halves the risk of skin cancer returning

modals.2026-10-23-health-4:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Health Digest · science

Study estimates summer heat killed more than 50,000 in Europe's cities

The modeling study estimated 50,391 excess heat-related deaths in 854 cities across 30 European countries this summer and attributed 32,619 of them to human-caused warming. The cities hold about 40% of those countries' population, so the figure does not cover all of Europe.

The researchers note the numbers are modeled estimates rather than counted deaths. They say the toll may be understated because the study leaves out heat in May and relies on coarse temperature data.

Why it matters: The estimate covers hundreds of cities and links most of this summer's heat deaths there to human-caused warming rather than natural variation.

  2. Record summer heat, mostly from climate change, kills 50,000 in Europe

modals.2026-10-23-health-5:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Health Digest · public-health

France reports first known human case of livestock Shamonda virus

The patient was being treated for a serious illness at a hospital in Lyon and had neurological complications that officials said were "very likely linked" to the virus, France's health and agriculture ministries said. They believe the infection came from a midge bite in eastern France, where the virus had been found in animals. Its role in the death is still under investigation.

Shamonda mainly affects cattle and is spread by biting midges. WHO confirmed it was the first documented human case and said the case appears isolated and unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time.

Why it matters: The virus had only been seen in animals despite decades of circulation in Africa and Asia. This year it has been found in farm animals in several European countries, including Ireland, Germany, Italy and Spain.

  1. Virus Shamonda: une première détection chez l'être humain
    French Ministry of Health · sante.gouv.fr · 2026-10-23
  2. First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say
    BBC · bbc.com · 2026-10-23
  3. Severely ill patient in France becomes first ever human infected with Shamonda virus
    ECDC · ecdc.europa.eu · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-25-wk-7:
Sunday · Oct 25, 2026 · Weekend Digest · public-health

Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from Congo

Uganda says it has no active Ebola infections after declaring its last outbreak over in July, but two people who later tested positive in Kenya and Nigeria had passed through the country, Reuters and AP reported. Screening has been stepped up at Entebbe International Airport and land borders, and all incoming travelers must fill in a passenger locator form.

Swiss authorities have said the woman diagnosed in Nigeria was infected in Uganda. Baryomunsi disputed that, saying relatives who had visited Congo met her in Kampala, and said "we should speak science, not politics," according to Reuters and Al Jazeera. He said all 60 contacts linked to Kenya's case had completed 21-day monitoring.

Why it matters: Congo's outbreak is the largest ever recorded in the country, with 4,687 deaths as of Oct. 20, according to World Health Organization figures cited by Bloomberg.

  2. Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from Congo

  3. Uganda orders 21-day Ebola quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo

modals.2026-10-26-health-1:
Monday · Oct 26, 2026 · Health Digest · public-health

Nigeria's Ebola patient flown to Switzerland as Africa CDC sends scientists to trace her infection

A Rega air ambulance flew the patient from Abuja to Zurich on Monday, Swiss news agency Keystone-SDA reported, and the University Hospital of Zurich said it had admitted a person with suspected Ebola. Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said her condition had improved and she was stable, but cautioned that she may still be infectious. Her husband, who has no symptoms, traveled with her. Nigerian authorities have identified 53 close contacts.

Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya told Reuters that a team led by Ebola co-discoverer Jean-Jacques Muyembe will travel to Abuja to work out how she caught the Bundibugyo virus. Her travel documents show she did not visit Congo, the center of the outbreak, he said. Genomic sequencing showed her virus was closely related to that of Kenya's first patient, though Kaseya said that does not mean one infected the other.
